title: Can I Ask for Consent to Search the Car?
summary: New Jersey rules for motor vehicle consent searches.

stop.q: Was the stop lawful (reasonable suspicion of a violation or crime)?

pc.q: Did probable cause to search arise spontaneously and unforeseeably at the scene?
pc.help: For example, contraband in plain view during the stop.

ras.q: Do you have reasonable, articulable suspicion that a search will reveal evidence of a crime?
ras.help: Required before even asking for consent (State v. Carty).

points: A warrantless roadside search is allowed when probable cause arises spontaneously and unforeseeably (State v. Witt).
No consent needed. Document the facts that created probable cause.
If the car is towed first, get a warrant.
Tell the person they have the right to refuse.
They may withdraw consent and may watch the search.
Use your agency's consent-to-search form and record on BWC.
Without reasonable suspicion, a consent request is not allowed in NJ.
Finish the stop without extending it.
Without reasonable suspicion, the stop and anything found may be suppressed.

note: Follow your department's policy and current AG directives. Not yet verified against official sources.
